steps.message:
Diagnosis confirmed. Let me explain the defect chain before patching:

**Root cause:** `DocumentIO.saveDocument()` decides whether to write to disk by comparing the editor text against the *in-memory* "initial version" (`Document.getInitialVersion()`), which is unreliable:

1. Editor history is **disabled by default** (`AppSettings.isEditorHistoryEnabled()` → `false`), so the snapshot `DocumentEditFragment.loadDocument()` tries to take (`document.addToHistory()`) is a **no-op** — `_history` stays empty.
2. After `HISTORY_DELTA` (5 s) the delayed runnable in `onContentEditValueChanged()` runs `_document.setContent(editorText)` — this is also what enables the save icon ("wait for the save icon to be enabled").
3. Pressing save → `getInitialVersion()` sees an empty history, so it **lazily snapshots the current document** (which already contains the typed text) and returns it as the "initial" version.
4. `!currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())` is therefore `false` → **the file is never written**, while `true` (success) is returned. All subsequent saves (onPause/back) compare against that same bogus `_history.get(0)` → never write.

If back is pressed within 5 s, `_document`'s content is still `""` when the snapshot is taken → contents differ → file gets written. That's precisely why skipping steps 3–4 works.

steps.message: The project lives inside a git-ignored `runs/` directory of an outer repo, so `git diff` is empty — here is the final state of both changed regions:

Done. The project compiles (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`) and the bug is fixed.

## Diagnosis

The save button didn't just fail to save — **it actively poisoned every later save attempt**, including the one on back/`onPause` that normally creates the note.

`DocumentIO.saveDocument()` decided whether to touch the disk by comparing the editor text against the *in-memory* "initial version": `!currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())`. That baseline is fabricated on demand:

1. `AppSettings.isEditorHistoryEnabled()` defaults to **`false`**, so the snapshot `DocumentEditFragment.loadDocument()` takes via `document.addToHistory()` is a **no-op** (`addToHistory()` is gated on `_doHistory`) → `_history` stays empty.
2. After `HISTORY_DELTA` (5 s) the delayed runnable in `onContentEditValueChanged()` runs `_document.setContent(editorText)`. This is also exactly what un-greys the save icon (`enable = !(content.isEmpty() || title.isEmpty())`) — i.e. *the icon only becomes usable once the state that breaks saving exists*.
3. Pressing save → `Document.getInitialVersion()` finds an empty history and **lazily snapshots the current document**, which already holds the typed text, then returns it as `_history.get(0)`.
4. `currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())` → `true` → no write, yet `true` (success) returned. Every subsequent save compares against that same bogus `_history.get(0)`, so back/`onPause` never writes either.

Pressing back within 5 s means `_document`'s content is still `""` when the snapshot is taken → contents differ → file written. That's exactly the reporter's "works if I skip steps 3 and 4".

## Patch

**`DocumentIO.java`** — the write decision now consults the only authority on whether a write is needed, the file itself (`!exists() || disk content != text`), with the in-memory/history sync kept as a separate concern.

**`DocumentEditFragment.java`** — the initial-version snapshot at load time is now taken regardless of the undo/redo preference (temporarily forcing `setDoHistory(true)`), restoring the invariant that `getInitialVersion()` reflects the state the document was *loaded* in rather than a mutated one.

## Verification

Since this logic is pure Java, I extracted `Document` plus the old/new save logic into a throwaway harness (removed afterwards) and replayed the reported gesture sequence:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| type, **wait, press save**, back (bug repro) | **NOT CREATED** | CREATED |
| type, back within 5 s (reporter's workaround) | CREATED | CREATED |
| edit existing note, wait, save, back | **CHANGES LOST** | SAVED |
| change title → rename on save | RENAMED ok | RENAMED ok |

Both preference states (`editorHistoryEnabled` true/false) pass after the patch, and the fix uncovered that the same defect silently **discarded edits to existing notes** — not only new-note creation. Rename-on-save behaviour is unchanged.

extra.final_message:
Done. The project compiles (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`) and the bug is fixed.

## Diagnosis

The save button didn't just fail to save — **it actively poisoned every later save attempt**, including the one on back/`onPause` that normally creates the note.

`DocumentIO.saveDocument()` decided whether to touch the disk by comparing the editor text against the *in-memory* "initial version": `!currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())`. That baseline is fabricated on demand:

1. `AppSettings.isEditorHistoryEnabled()` defaults to **`false`**, so the snapshot `DocumentEditFragment.loadDocument()` takes via `document.addToHistory()` is a **no-op** (`addToHistory()` is gated on `_doHistory`) → `_history` stays empty.
2. After `HISTORY_DELTA` (5 s) the delayed runnable in `onContentEditValueChanged()` runs `_document.setContent(editorText)`. This is also exactly what un-greys the save icon (`enable = !(content.isEmpty() || title.isEmpty())`) — i.e. *the icon only becomes usable once the state that breaks saving exists*.
3. Pressing save → `Document.getInitialVersion()` finds an empty history and **lazily snapshots the current document**, which already holds the typed text, then returns it as `_history.get(0)`.
4. `currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())` → `true` → no write, yet `true` (success) returned. Every subsequent save compares against that same bogus `_history.get(0)`, so back/`onPause` never writes either.

Pressing back within 5 s means `_document`'s content is still `""` when the snapshot is taken → contents differ → file written. That's exactly the reporter's "works if I skip steps 3 and 4".

## Patch

**`DocumentIO.java`** — the write decision now consults the only authority on whether a write is needed, the file itself (`!exists() || disk content != text`), with the in-memory/history sync kept as a separate concern.

**`DocumentEditFragment.java`** — the initial-version snapshot at load time is now taken regardless of the undo/redo preference (temporarily forcing `setDoHistory(true)`), restoring the invariant that `getInitialVersion()` reflects the state the document was *loaded* in rather than a mutated one.

## Verification

Since this logic is pure Java, I extracted `Document` plus the old/new save logic into a throwaway harness (removed afterwards) and replayed the reported gesture sequence:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| type, **wait, press save**, back (bug repro) | **NOT CREATED** | CREATED |
| type, back within 5 s (reporter's workaround) | CREATED | CREATED |
| edit existing note, wait, save, back | **CHANGES LOST** | SAVED |
| change title → rename on save | RENAMED ok | RENAMED ok |

Both preference states (`editorHistoryEnabled` true/false) pass after the patch, and the fix uncovered that the same defect silently **discarded edits to existing notes** — not only new-note creation. Rename-on-save behaviour is unchanged.
